description: The sidebar's navigation list -- the list alone, not the frame around it.

items.description: The destinations, in order. Required, and guarded at runtime against ABSENCE only: an empty array is a caller saying "no destinations right now" and renders an empty landmark, which is legal. Omitting the member entirely is the omission that throws.

active.description: The `id` of the current destination. Marks that item aria-current="page", and no item is marked when it names none of them.

ariaLabel.description: Names this navigation landmark. Required, and guarded at runtime rather than defaulted: the navigation pattern asks each landmark on a page for a UNIQUE name, and a constant default satisfies the existence half while two sidebars on one page stay indistinguishable -- which is the defect Pagination.behaviour.json's roles.label exception records for the sibling component. Nothing can derive it either; what a nav is FOR is editorial. Say what it navigates -- "Primary", "Project settings" -- the Table.label and SegmentedControl.ariaLabel shape.

nav.description: An item was activated, carrying that item alone. The native MouseEvent is not forwarded, so a listener cannot call preventDefault() on the anchor's own navigation -- ctrl-click, middle-click and open-in-new-tab still work for a consumer who wires nothing; intercepting a plain click to substitute SPA routing belongs at the router (routerLink, Link), not here.
